Title: NPM Scripts You Should Stop Writing Manually
Desc: Learn how to use NPM scripts to automate repetitive development tasks, improve productivity, and simplify project workflows without installing unnecessary tools.
Author: Pro Bandey
Data:
## Many developers waste time repeating the same terminal commands every day.

Examples:

```text
Start Development Server
Run Tests
Format Code
Build Project
Lint Files
```
Typing these commands repeatedly becomes tedious.

That's exactly why NPM scripts exist.

---

## What Are NPM Scripts?

NPM scripts are commands defined inside your project's:

```text id="pkg-file"
package.json
```

They allow you to run complex commands using simple shortcuts.

Instead of:

```bash id="long-command"
npx vite --host --port 3000
```

You can run:

```bash id="short-command"
npm run dev
```

Much cleaner.

---

## Where NPM Scripts Live

Inside your `package.json` file:

```json id="package-json"
{
  "scripts": {
    "dev": "vite"
  }
}
```

Now:

```bash id="run-dev"
npm run dev
```

starts your development server.

---

## Why Use NPM Scripts?

Benefits include:

- Faster workflow
- Consistent commands
- Easier onboarding
- Less typing
- Better automation

Workflow:

```text id="automation"
Task
↓
Script
↓
One Command
```

## Script #1: Development Server

Many developers manually start development servers.

Instead:

```json id="dev-script"
{
  "scripts": {
    "dev": "vite"
  }
}
```

Run:

```bash id="dev-run"
npm run dev
```

Simple and memorable.

---

## Script #2: Production Build

Instead of remembering build commands:

```json id="build-script"
{
  "scripts": {
    "build": "vite build"
  }
}
```

Run:

```bash id="build-run"
npm run build
```

Works consistently across environments.

---

## Script #3: Preview Production Builds

For projects using Vite:

```json id="preview-script"
{
  "scripts": {
    "preview": "vite preview"
  }
}
```

Run:

```bash id="preview-run"
npm run preview
```

Useful for final verification.

---

## Script #4: Run Tests

Testing should be easy.

Example:

```json id="test-script"
{
  "scripts": {
    "test": "vitest"
  }
}
```

Run:

```bash id="run-test"
npm test
```

No need to remember lengthy commands.

---

## Script #5: Watch Tests Automatically

Example:

```json id="test-watch"
{
  "scripts": {
    "test:watch": "vitest --watch"
  }
}
```

Run:

```bash id="watch-tests"
npm run test:watch
```

Tests rerun automatically when files change.

---

![Automated testing and continuous development workflow](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1526379095098-d400fd0bf935)

## Script #6: Lint Your Code

Linting improves code quality.

Example:

```json id="lint-script"
{
  "scripts": {
    "lint": "eslint ."
  }
}
```

Run:

```bash id="run-lint"
npm run lint
```

Catch issues early.

---

## Script #7: Auto-Fix Lint Problems

Example:

```json id="lint-fix"
{
  "scripts": {
    "lint:fix": "eslint . --fix"
  }
}
```

Run:

```bash id="run-lint-fix"
npm run lint:fix
```

Saves significant cleanup time.

---

## Script #8: Format Code

Using Prettier:

```json id="format-script"
{
  "scripts": {
    "format": "prettier . --write"
  }
}
```

Run:

```bash id="run-format"
npm run format
```

Consistent formatting becomes effortless.

---

## Script #9: Clean Build Directories

Instead of deleting folders manually:

```json id="clean-script"
{
  "scripts": {
    "clean": "rm -rf dist"
  }
}
```

Run:

```bash id="clean-run"
npm run clean
```

Useful before rebuilding projects.

---

## Script #10: Build and Deploy

Combine commands:

```json id="deploy-script"
{
  "scripts": {
    "deploy": "npm run build && npm run upload"
  }
}
```

Workflow:

```text id="deploy-flow"
Build
↓
Upload
↓
Deploy
```

One command handles everything.

---

## Script Chaining

NPM scripts can call other scripts.

Example:

```json id="chain-script"
{
  "scripts": {
    "lint": "eslint .",
    "test": "vitest",
    "check": "npm run lint && npm run test"
  }
}
```

Run:

```bash id="check-run"
npm run check
```

This executes multiple tasks automatically.

---

## Useful Script Naming Conventions

Common conventions:

```text id="naming"
dev
build
preview
test
lint
lint:fix
format
clean
deploy
```

Most developers recognize these names instantly.

---

## Example Real-World Setup

```json id="real-world"
{
  "scripts": {
    "dev": "vite",
    "build": "vite build",
    "preview": "vite preview",
    "test": "vitest",
    "lint": "eslint .",
    "lint:fix": "eslint . --fix",
    "format": "prettier . --write"
  }
}
```

This setup covers most modern frontend projects.

---

## Common Mistakes

### Creating Overly Complex Scripts

Keep scripts focused and readable.

---

### Using Inconsistent Names

Standard naming improves team collaboration.

---

### Duplicating Commands

Reuse scripts whenever possible.

---

### Skipping Automation

If a command runs often, it probably deserves a script.

---

## Signs a Task Should Become an NPM Script

Ask yourself:

```text id="script-test"
Do I Run This Command
More Than Once A Week?
```

If yes, automate it.

---

## Benefits for Teams

NPM scripts improve:

- Consistency
- Onboarding
- Documentation
- Productivity
- Collaboration

Every developer runs the same commands.

No guessing required.

---

## FAQ

### Are NPM scripts only for Node.js projects?

They are most common in Node.js projects but can run any shell command.

### Can scripts call other scripts?

Yes. This is a common practice.

### Why use scripts instead of typing commands manually?

They save time and ensure consistency.

### Should every project have NPM scripts?

Most modern JavaScript projects benefit significantly from them.

### What is the most useful NPM script?

Usually `dev`, `build`, `test`, and `lint`.

---

## Final Thoughts

NPM scripts are one of the simplest productivity tools available to JavaScript developers.

Instead of repeatedly typing long commands, you can create reusable shortcuts that make development faster and more consistent.

The rule is simple:

```text
Repeated Task
↓
Automate It
↓
Save Time
```

If you're still manually running the same commands every day, it's probably time to turn them into NPM scripts.
